content.text:
Noted — I'm treating that as thinking aloud, not a request, so I haven't set anything up or changed the code.

My honest read on whether it would have helped here: probably not much, because the two things I flagged aren't questions a second model is better positioned to answer. "Should `Café` become `cafe` or `caf-`?" is a product decision about your URLs and your content — a reviewer with no more context than I have would just produce a differently-confident guess. Same for the dead `.trim()`. What resolves those is you, or a convention already in the codebase.

Where an outside check does earn its cost is a different shape of problem: a verifiable claim I could be confidently wrong about — a regex that misbehaves on an input class I didn't think to test, an API whose behavior changed after my cutoff, a perf or security assumption. Those have right answers, so a second pass can actually catch something rather than add a vote.

Two cheaper things that cover a lot of the same ground for edge cases like this: property-based tests (slug is idempotent, output matches `^[a-z0-9-]*$`, no leading/trailing dash) pin down behavior without needing anyone's opinion; and `/code-review` on the diff is already a fresh adversarial pass.

If you do want to formalize it later — a reviewer subagent on diffs, or a rule about when to escalate — tell me the trigger condition you have in mind and I'll wire it up and save it as a standing preference. I'd rather do that once you've decided than guess at a policy now.
